meta.indication: secondary prevention of cardiovascular events in stable (chronic) coronary heart disease

n_randomized.quote: In a double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 15,828 patients with stable coronary heart disease to receive either once-daily darapladib (at a dose of 160 mg) or placebo.
n_randomized.note: Also: registry enrollment 15828 ACTUAL (S3); design paper S2 (2010) already states 'The study has randomized 15,828 patients'.

median_followup.quote: The median duration of follow-up for the primary end point was 3.7 years (interquartile range, 3.5 to 3.8).
median_followup.location: Results, Follow-up, Adherence, and Background Therapy
median_followup.note: 3.7 years converted to months (3.7*12). Design anticipated median treatment duration 2.75 years (S2).

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (MACE)
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Stable chronic CHD (prior MI, prior PCI/CABG, or multivessel CAD) plus >=1 additional risk predictor (age >=60, diabetes on drugs, HDL-C <40 mg/dL, smoking >=5 cig/day, moderate renal dysfunction, or polyvascular disease); background statin expected
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients were eligible to participate in the study if they had coronary heart disease, as documented by at least one of the following: previous myocardial infarction, previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary-artery bypass grafting (CABG), or multivessel coronary artery disease. In addition, at least one of the following additional predictors of cardiovascular risk was required: an age of 60 years or older, diabetes requiring pharmacotherapy, a high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol level of less than 40 mg per deciliter (1.03 mmol per liter), status as a smoker of five or more cigarettes per day at study entry or within 3 months before screening, moderate renal dysfunction, or polyvascular arterial disease.

planned_events.quote: We then estimated that 1500 events would be required for the study to have a power of 90% to detect a relative-risk reduction of 15.5% in the rate of the primary end point in the darapladib group, as compared with the placebo group.
planned_events.note: Same in design paper abstract S2 (2010): 'The study will continue until 1,500 primary end points have occurred to achieve 90% power to detect a 15.5% reduction in the primary end point.' Assumed annual placebo event rate 4%. Observed: 1588 primary events (769+819).

assumed_rrr.quote: We then estimated that 1500 events would be required for the study to have a power of 90% to detect a relative-risk reduction of 15.5% in the rate of the primary end point in the darapladib group, as compared with the placebo group.

power.quote: We then estimated that 1500 events would be required for the study to have a power of 90% to detect a relative-risk reduction of 15.5% in the rate of the primary end point in the darapladib group, as compared with the placebo group.

alpha.quote: The effect of treatment on the primary end point was estimated with the use of hazard ratios and adjusted 95.1% confidence intervals, with a two-sided P value of 0.049 indicating statistical significance after adjustment for the four interim analyses conducted by the data and safety monitoring committee.
alpha.note: Overall nominal alpha 0.05 two-sided, final threshold 0.049 after 4 interim analyses (2 prespecified, 2 unplanned).

stopped_early.quote: During a median follow-up period of 3.7 years, the primary end point occurred in 769 of 7924 patients (9.7%) in the darapladib group and 819 of 7904 patients (10.4%) in the placebo group
stopped_early.note: Not stopped early; ran to planned event target (1588 of 1500 planned primary events observed).

baseline.quote: The median low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol level at baseline was 79.9 mg per deciliter (2.07 mmol per liter).

At 1 month, the Lp‐PLA 2 activity was reduced from a median of 172 to 57 μmol/min per liter (interquartile range 42–75 μmol/min per liter, mean reduction 112 μmol/min per liter, mean percentage reduction 64%) in the darapladib group compared with a median decrease from 173 to 164 μmol/min per liter (interquartile range 136–196 μmol/min per liter, mean reduction 9 μmol/min per liter, mean percentage reduction 4%) in the placebo group.
baseline.note: Median baseline 172 (darapladib) / 173 (placebo). NOT reported in the main NEJM paper: 'Baseline and on-treatment lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 levels are not yet available and thus are not reported here.' Published 2016, after readout.

biomarker_effects.method: plasma Lp-PLA2 enzyme activity, central lab
biomarker_effects.quote: At 1 month, the Lp‐PLA 2 activity was reduced from a median of 172 to 57 μmol/min per liter (interquartile range 42–75 μmol/min per liter, mean reduction 112 μmol/min per liter, mean percentage reduction 64%) in the darapladib group compared with a median decrease from 173 to 164 μmol/min per liter (interquartile range 136–196 μmol/min per liter, mean reduction 9 μmol/min per liter, mean percentage reduction 4%) in the placebo group.
biomarker_effects.note: Within-group mean % change; placebo -4%, so placebo-adjusted ~ -60 percentage points (derived). Paper summary: 'Darapladib treatment produced a persistent ≈65% relative reduction in Lp‐PLA 2 activity from the first on‐treatment measurement at 1 month until study termination'. The commonly cited -65% matches. Not available at readout (published 2016-06-21). NEJM design assumption: 'The assigned dose of darapladib was expected to lower plasma levels of lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 by approximately 60%.'

biomarker_effects.quote: The median LDL cholesterol level at the end of the study was 78.0 mg per deciliter (2.02 mmol per liter) in the darapladib group and 78.8 mg per deciliter (2.04 mmol per liter) in the placebo group.
biomarker_effects.note: change_abs is the derived between-group difference in end-of-study medians; i.e., no LDL effect.

biomarker_effects.quote: Darapladib 40, 80, and 160 mg inhibited Lp-PLA(2) activity by approximately 43%, 55%, and 66% compared with placebo (p < 0.001 weeks 4 and 12).
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 2 dose-ranging, n=959 CHD/CHD-risk-equivalent patients on atorvastatin 20 or 80 mg. 160 mg = phase 3 dose.

biomarker_effects.quote: At 12 weeks, darapladib 160 mg decreased interleukin (IL)-6 by 12.3% (95% confidence interval [CI] -22% to -1%; p = 0.028) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) by 13.0% (95% CI -28% to +5%; p = 0.15) compared with placebo.
In contrast, Lp-PLA(2) activity was inhibited by 59% with darapladib (P<0.001 versus placebo).
biomarker_effects.note: IBIS-2, n=330 angiographic CAD. Primary end points (plaque deformability P=0.22; hs-CRP P=0.35) were NOT met; secondary necrotic core volume treatment difference -5.2 mm3 (P=0.012) with no difference in total atheroma volume (P=0.95).

biomarker_effects.quote: In the placebo-treated group, however, necrotic core volume increased significantly (4.5+/-17.9 mm(3); P=0.009), whereas darapladib halted this increase (-0.5+/-13.9 mm(3); P=0.71), resulting in a significant treatment difference of -5.2 mm(3) (P=0.012).
biomarker_effects.note: Secondary end point; the main efficacy signal used to justify phase 3.

hr.quote: (hazard ratio in the darapladib group, 0.94; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.03; P=0.20)
hr.note: Registry (S3) reports HR 0.94 with 95.1% CI 0.85-1.03, p=0.199.

ci_low.quote: (hazard ratio in the darapladib group, 0.94; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.03; P=0.20)
ci_low.note: Methods specify adjusted 95.1% CI for the primary end point.

ci_high.quote: (hazard ratio in the darapladib group, 0.94; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.03; P=0.20)

p.location: ClinicalTrials.gov results, primary outcome statistical analysis
p.note: NEJM reports P=0.20; GSK press release (S4) 'p=0.199'.

events_treatment.quote: the primary end point occurred in 769 of 7924 patients (9.7%) in the darapladib group

events_control.quote: 819 of 7904 patients (10.4%) in the placebo group

safety_signals.value: Major coronary events nominally reduced (secondary end point)
safety_signals.quote: Darapladib, as compared with placebo, reduced the rate of major coronary events (9.3% vs. 10.3%; hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82 to 1.00; P=0.045) and total coronary events (14.6% vs. 16.1%; hazard ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.84 to 0.98; P=0.02).
safety_signals.note: Efficacy signal, not safety; recorded because it drove the SOLID-TIMI 52 primary end point change. Nominal (unadjusted).

safety_signals.value: Odor (feces, urine, skin) and diarrhea led to more discontinuations
safety_signals.quote: More patients in the darapladib group than in the placebo group discontinued the study drug because of diarrhea (3.2% vs. 0.8%), feces odor (2.2% vs. 0.1%), urine odor (1.4% vs. <0.1%), and skin odor (2.2% vs. 0.1%).
safety_signals.note: Overall study-drug discontinuation 32.7% vs 26.8% (HR 1.29); AE-related discontinuation 19.8% vs 13.5%.

safety_signals.value: Renal failure serious adverse events increased
safety_signals.quote: There were more serious adverse events of renal failure in the darapladib group than in the placebo group (1.5% vs. 1.1%; hazard ratio, 1.35; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.78).
safety_signals.note: eGFR ~2 ml/min/1.73m2 lower on treatment; no difference after end of treatment in a 2650-patient subgroup.

genetics.finding: PLA2G7 V279F (loss-of-function, 'm' allele) was MORE frequent in Japanese patients with MI or stroke than in controls (candidate-gene case-control, n=3932); direction opposite to the darapladib hypothesis
genetics.effect: qualitative; no effect size in abstract
genetics.quote: We observed a significantly increased frequency of the m allele in the diseased group as compared with the control or risk-factor groups.
genetics.note: Small early East Asian candidate-gene study; abstract read on PubMed. Later East Asian V279F studies were pooled in Gregson 2017.

genetics.finding: Common PLA2G7 variants have only small effects on Lp-PLA2 activity (weak instrument) and showed no association with CHD; authors state they could not exclude a modest causal effect
genetics.effect: rs1051931 (A379V) VV vs AA: +7.2% Lp-PLA2 activity; CHD events OR 0.98 (95% CI 0.82-1.17); angiographic CAD OR 1.03 (0.80-1.32)
genetics.quote: Genotype was not associated with risk markers, angiographic coronary disease (odds ratio, 1.03; 95% confidence interval, 0.80 to 1.32), or CHD events (odds ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval, 0.82 to 1.17).
genetics.note: Weak-instrument caveat in the Discussion (PMC author manuscript): 'a per-allele OR as low as 1.05 (which we were insufficiently powered to detect) could still be compatible with a contributory role of Lp-PLA2 to CHD.' Abstract also: 'Larger association studies, identification of single-nucleotide polymorphisms with larger effects, or randomized trials of specific Lp-PLA2 inhibitors are needed'.

genetics.finding: PLA2G7 V279F loss-of-function variant (lifelong lower Lp-PLA2) not associated with major vascular events or major coronary events in 91,428 China Kadoorie Biobank participants
genetics.effect: Major vascular events OR 0.98 per F allele (95% CI 0.90-1.06); major coronary events OR 0.96 (0.79-1.18)
genetics.quote: V279F was not associated with major vascular events [7141 events; odds ratio (OR) = 0.98 per F variant, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.90-1.06] or other vascular outcomes, including major coronary events (922 events; 0.96, 0.79-1.18) and stroke (5967 events; 1.00, 0.92-1.09).
genetics.note: Published in Int J Epidemiol (not JAMA Cardiol); post-dates both darapladib readouts.

genetics.finding: Large-scale genetic invalidation: none of five Lp-PLA2-lowering PLA2G7 alleles associated with CHD; genetic causal risk ratio per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity matches the null darapladib trial estimate
genetics.effect: CHD RR per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity: Val279Phe 0.95 (0.88-1.03); any LoF 0.92 (0.74-1.16); Val379Ala 1.01 (0.68-1.51); darapladib trials 0.95 (0.89-1.02)
genetics.quote: Causal risk ratios for coronary heart disease per 65% lower Lp-PLA2 activity were: 0.95 (0.88-1.03) with Val279Phe; 0.92 (0.74-1.16) with carriage of any loss-of-function variant; 1.01 (0.68-1.51) with Val379Ala; and 0.95 (0.89-1.02) with darapladib treatment.
genetics.note: Online first 2016-12-08; post-dates both darapladib readouts.

consensus_explanation.summary: Darapladib achieved the intended pharmacology (~65% persistent reduction in plasma Lp-PLA2 activity in ~14,500 STABILITY patients) yet did not reduce MACE, and the degree of Lp-PLA2 lowering did not relate to outcomes. Large human-genetic studies published afterwards (Millwood 2016, V279F in China Kadoorie Biobank; Gregson 2017, five PLA2G7 loss-of-function/lowering alleles in ~120,000 CHD cases) found no association of genetically lower Lp-PLA2 activity with CHD, with a causal risk ratio per 65% lower activity (~0.95) matching the null trial. The accepted explanation is that plasma Lp-PLA2 is a marker of risk, not a causal driver (target invalid). The only pre-trial genetic evidence (Casas 2010) used weak instruments (~7% activity difference) and could not test causality, so the program rested on observational association and a secondary IVUS necrotic-core signal in IBIS-2 (primary end points of IBIS-2 were negative). High background statin use and a nominal reduction in major coronary events were discussed but are not considered the reason for failure.

pre_readout.note: Readout = GSK top-line press release 2013-11-12 (S4). Items listed with source pub_date.
available_before_readout: Design: N 15,828, 1,500 events, 90% power, 15.5% RRR, MACE primary end point (S2 American Heart Journal, 2010-10-01; abstract free)
Registry record with eligibility (S3, first posted 2008-12)
Phase 2 Lp-PLA2 inhibition ~66% at 160 mg vs placebo; hs-CRP -13% (NS) (S7 Mohler, JACC 2008-04-29)
IBIS-2: Lp-PLA2 -59% at 12 months; primary end points (plaque deformability, hs-CRP) negative; necrotic core -5.2 mm3 (secondary) (S8, Circulation 2008-09-01)
Genetics: Casas 2010 (S9, 2010-05-17) - weak PLA2G7 instruments (rs1051931 ~7% activity), null for CHD, underpowered
Genetics: Yamada 2000 (S12) - V279F loss-of-function enriched in Japanese MI/stroke patients (direction against hypothesis)
only_after_readout: Full results, HR 0.94 (0.85-1.03), events 769 vs 819, median follow-up 3.7 y (S1 NEJM, 2014-03-30; S5 GSK 2014-03-30)
On-treatment Lp-PLA2 reduction in STABILITY (~65%) and baseline Lp-PLA2 (S6 Wallentin JAHA, 2016-06-21)
Genetics: Millwood 2016 (S10, 2016-06-14) and Gregson 2017 (S11, online 2016-12-08) - genetic invalidation of Lp-PLA2

access_summary.note: Counted by best free access. Key numbers: N, median follow-up, planned events, RRR, power, alpha, HR, CI low, CI high, p, events x2, baseline LDL-C (NEJM S1, read as full text in a browser; also all trial-level outcome numbers are in the free abstract and registry results S3), baseline + on-treatment Lp-PLA2 (PMC open S6), phase 2 Lp-PLA2 (S7) and IBIS-2 Lp-PLA2 (S8) from free PubMed abstracts. If NEJM full text is treated as not freely machine-accessible (Cloudflare bot check), planned events/power/RRR remain free via the S2 abstract, and alpha (0.049) becomes paywalled-only.

open_questions: Access of NEJM full text (S1): full text was readable in a browser on 2026-10-05 without visible login (NEJM makes research free 6 months after publication), but WebFetch/curl get HTTP 403 and a later browser visit hit a Cloudflare bot check. Europe PMC lists it as not open access, no PMC copy. Classified open_full_text with this caveat.
GSK top-line release (S4) reported 'relative risk reduction of 6%; p=0.199' without HR/CI or event counts; those first appeared 2014-03-30 (S1/S5).

Commonly cited 'Lp-PLA2 activity -65%' for STABILITY is NOT in the NEJM paper (levels 'not yet available'); it comes from Wallentin 2016 (S6, within-group ~65%, placebo -4%) and Gregson 2017 pooled trials (S11, '160 mg once-daily darapladib reduced Lp-PLA2 activity by 65%'). Placebo-adjusted value ~ -60 percentage points at 1 month (derived).
Total coronary events: NEJM abstract says 14.6% vs 16.1%; GSK release (S5) says 14.9% vs 16.1%, p=0.019. Minor discrepancy.
Median follow-up stored in months (44.4) converted from 3.7 years; registry gives 'up to 4.25 years/average of 3.51 years'.
NEJM Table 3 adverse event incidence for odor/diarrhea (not discontinuation) not extracted as text.
